title: Per-day rolls from SimRng.stateless may be more regular than intended
tier_reason: Sim-layer code behind tests and the replay round-trip; git reverts it. Changing the derivation changes existing seeds' days, so it must be versioned or replays of old sessions diverge.
ask: Found 2026-09-09 while building the Mark III's policy sampler: SimRng.stateless(salt, index) hashes the string 'seed:salt:index', and Godot's string hash moves by exactly one when the index moves by one, so consecutive indices give consecutive hash values (measured: 62% of 5,000 draws in one tenth of the range). Every per-day roll that takes stateless(...) % n over a running index — crow schedules, ant schedules, visitor schedules, crow targets — may therefore cycle rather than vary. Check whether the schedules a player sees are regular enough to predict (the CEO rejects anything that reads as a pattern), and if so, scramble the index before hashing the way Policy.draw_u does — behind a replay-format or save-version guard so old logs still replay.
first_action: Print 30 days of roll_crow_schedule and roll_visitor_schedules for three seeds and look for cycles; then decide whether stateless itself changes (with a versioned guard) or only new callers use Policy.draw_u.
source_message: Chief of staff session 2026-09-09: WI-2 worker's finding while building the Mark III sampler.
result: Commit bdbbe00 already fixes the predictable per-day crow schedule. The Godot measurement tool printed 30 days for seeds 1, 42, and 20260909 under both revisions: each legacy seed has a +9 crow timing step on 24 of 27 transitions; each current seed's most frequent step occurs only four times. Visitor schedules are empty on all 30 days because shipping visitor counts are zero. Fresh farms use stateless revision 2; v5 saves and v2 seed replays retain revision 1; v6 saves and v3 replays carry the current revision, with continued replays inheriting their base save. Local unit suite: 2,946 passed, 0 failed. Local integration suite: 999 passed, 0 failed. Main CI run 36004431062 passed at 3e19899, which contains bdbbe00. A newer run at 1531c7b7 is queued; the separate CI-failure card owns failed run 36002749160.
